title: Kitchener Rangers Aud renovation and Enova board appointments
subtitle: Council also named Enova directors, extended independent director terms, and authorized a closed session on land disposition.
overview: Council approved the Kitchener Rangers' request to renovate the players' dressing room area, business office and media/scouts room at Kitchener Memorial Auditorium Complex (The Aud) {{vote:m2}}. The Rangers will lead the work, including hiring architects and contractors, with ongoing project support from the City.

At the same time, the City will build a restaurant at The Aud, with $2,000,000 approved for it. The stated aim is to improve the fan experience and make the facility more attractive for major events, large concerts and tournaments. One councillor declared a conflict and did not take part in the matter.

Council also filled its seats on the boards of the Enova hydro companies. One councillor goes to the Enova Power Corp. board and two go to the Enova Energy Corporation board, starting June 1, 2025, for terms of up to one year {{vote:m1}}. The terms of the two independent directors were extended by a year, to 2026. Council then authorized a closed session on a potential land disposition {{vote:m3}}.
The meeting lasted about six minutes.

decisions.item: Kitchener Rangers renovation at The Aud
decisions.detail: Council approved the Rangers' request to renovate the players' dressing room area, business office and media/scouts room, led by the Rangers with City project management support.
Council directed the City to build a restaurant at The Aud alongside the renovations and approved $2,000,000 in funding for it.
Councillor S. Davey was appointed to the Enova Power Corp. board effective June 1, 2025, for a term of up to one year.
Councillors P. Singh and D. Chapman were appointed to the Enova Energy Corporation board effective June 1, 2025, for terms of up to one year.
The terms of the City's two independent Enova Energy Corporation directors, Don McKinnon and Jim Philips, were extended by one year to conclude in 2026.

debate: Debate was minimal. On the Aud renovation, the chair asked for discussion and one councillor said everything had already been said at the committee meeting earlier that day.
On the Enova appointments, several councillors were nominated for the three seats, and one nominee declined. That left three nominees for three positions.
Councillors noted that which person sits on the Enova Power Corp. board and which on the Enova Energy Corporation board made little practical difference, and they settled the split quickly.
The transcript records no concerns from delegates, because none were registered for the meeting.
